messages:
lena: Hey team — customer says their April invoice total doesn't match the sum of line items after VAT. They see a -0.01 discrepancy in EUR. attaching sample csv and the invoice id: INV-2026-0427-88

lena: CSV snippet:
```
line_item_id,amount,currency,vat_pct,prorated_amount
li_101,12.34,EUR,20,12.34
li_102,0.67,EUR,20,0.67
li_103,0.01,EUR,20,0.01
subtotal,13.02,EUR,,
vat,2.60,EUR,,
invoice_total,15.62,EUR,,
ledger_total,15.61,EUR,, <-- customer ledger export shows this
```

lena: They say dashboard shows 15.62, invoice PDF shows 15.62, but exported ledger (for accounting) is 15.61. Customer is worried about audit trail.

omar: Thanks — can you confirm whether VAT is calculated per-line then rounded, or calculated on subtotal? Also which export they used for ledger (CSV vs GL export)?

lena: They used the "billing ledger export" from account settings -> billing -> export. Per their note, ledger rows are per-request aggregated into lineitems then rounded to cents.

sree: Quick hypothesis: we may be rounding each prorated item to cents at a different stage than the ledger export. There's a known edge-case when we convert EUR -> microcents, do math, then round back. If we do per-request rounding early and then sum, vs summing raw micros then rounding once, you can get +/- 1 cent.

sree: Repro script I used locally: 
```bash
python repro_round.py --items "12.34,0.67,0.01" --vat 0.20 --currency EUR
# repro_round.py sums in micros, applies VAT then rounds once vs per-line round
```

sree: Output: single-round -> total 1562 cents; per-line-round -> total 1561 cents.

miguel: From accounting POV we need deterministic invoice->ledger reconciliation strategy. Which behavior matches legal invoice (PDF)? We should prefer PDF math: compute subtotal, compute VAT on subtotal, round VAT, then sum. If ledger export does per-line rounding we need to change it or add a flag to indicate rounding policy.

billing-bot: automated-check: rounding-audit ran on INV-2026-0427-88: detected 1c mismatch between invoice_pdf and ledger_export. Flagged for review.

omar: Proposed next steps: 1) confirm rounding policy in config for that account (self-serve vs enterprise). 2) run a backfill script to detect invoices with nonzero discrepancy last 6 months. 3) offer customer credit if material or explain immaterial 1c differences.

lena: I've checked account config — default policy is "per-invoice VAT" (subtotal -> VAT). The ledger export pipeline appears to apply per-line rounding at aggregation time.

sree: I'll open a PR to make ledger export use the same canonical rounding path (sum in smallest unit then single round for VAT). For short term we can add a note in export header about rounding policy. PR will include unit tests + repro fixture.

miguel: Also confirm multi-currency conversions: if invoice was generated after conversion from GBP -> EUR we need to ensure conversion happens before rounding. That can create further off-by-1's.

sree: Agreed. I'll add regression test for FX -> VAT ordering.

lena: Customer update plan: explain root cause, offer ledger re-export with a rounding-policy flag and a goodwill credit of 0.01 EUR if they prefer. Asking for approval to issue credit.

omar: Approve 0.01 EUR credit in this case. Also add a ticket to detect these proactively and surface them in Console billing alerts.

lena: Filed support ticket with customer, waiting on their acceptance for credit. Marking thread for follow-up after PR merges. :white_check_mark:
